title: Internal Hom finiteness for the existing small coefficient class
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime and let $k$ be a field of positive characteristic different from $\ell$. Let $X$ be separated of finite type over $k$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be one of the following condensed coefficient rings [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]: $\underline E$ for a finite normed extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with carrier in $\mathrm{Type}\,0$; $\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ for its closed unit ball or the valuation ring of a finite subextension of $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$; or $\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}$. For bounded constructible $K,L\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X})$ [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], the ambient derived internal Hom $R\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda_X}(K,L)$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] is bounded constructible. The coefficient cases are exactly the constructors of the existing Lean class IsEllAdicFinitenessCoefficient.

external.place: Since $K$ is bounded constructible, reduction modulo $\varpi$ gives $$ \RHom(K,L)/\varpi\cong\RHom_{\cO_E/\varpi}(K/\varpi,L/\varpi). $$ By Deligne's finiteness theorem for the internal $\RHom$ (SGA 4½, *Th. finitude*, 1.6) on the finite type $k$-scheme $X$, with coefficients in which $p$ is invertible, this is a bounded complex with constructible cohomology.

The cases $\underline E$ and $\underline{\Qlb}$ follow by inverting $\ell$ and by descending to a finite extension $E$ ([sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit]), as in [lem-sfb-dc-lower-star-preserves]; see Bhatt–Scholze, §6.8.

The cases $\underline E$ and $\underline{\Qlb}$ follow by inverting $\ell$ and by descending to a finite extension $E$ ([sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit]), as in [lem-sfb-dc-lower-star-preserves]; see Bhatt–Scholze, §6.8.

proof.text: For an abstract finite normed $E$, powers of each element are linearly dependent, so $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is algebraic. Choose an embedding into $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Uniqueness of the extended absolute value identifies its induced norm with the given norm, hence also identifies the closed unit balls and condensed coefficients. Work with this embedded $E$.

source.place: Tag 09GU, lemma-map-into-algebraic-closure; norm uniqueness is used only through lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value, with its source caveat retained.

proof.text: $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian (its ideals are $0,k$), hence so is $X$. Put $B=\mathcal O_{E,X}$, choose a uniformizer $t$, and put $A=\mathcal O_E/(t)$. The DVR lemma makes $A$ finite; its characteristic is $\ell$. The coefficient-limit lemma gives $B=\varprojlim_n(\mathcal O_E/t^n)_X$.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11 and coefficient inverse-limit description; Noetherian finite-type schemes: Stacks Tag 01T6, morphisms.tex, lemma-finite-type-noetherian, used through the cited node.

proof.text: For integral $K,L$, the integral model comparison changes general-lfp cohomology into finite scalar local models. The adic criterion, (1)$\Rightarrow$(2), gives local derived completeness and bounded constructible finite-Tor étale reductions $K_1,L_1$.

source.place: Definition 6.5.1 and Proposition 6.8.11(3), via the explicitly cited general-lfp comparison and cohomological adic criterion (Stacks Tag 09C0, proetale.tex, section-suitable-derived).

proof.text: For $H=R\mathcal Hom_B(K,L)$, reduction comparison gives $H\otimes_B^L A_X\simeq R\mathcal Hom_{A_X}(K_1,L_1)$, where $K_1=K\otimes_B^LA_X\simeq\nu_X^*C_K$ and $L_1\simeq\nu_X^*C_L$ for the étale complexes of step 3. Constructible comparison makes their cohomology finite scalar constructible. Finite-field Hom finiteness makes $H\otimes_B^LA_X$ bounded with finite scalar constructible cohomology. Local completeness of $L$ makes $H$ locally complete.

source.place: Lemma 3.4.11; reduction comparison of Lemma 6.7.13 used through lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction; local completeness through Stacks Tag 099A, algebraization.tex, lemma-derived-complete-internal-hom. Finite-field finiteness remains its separate cited obligation.

proof.text: Constructible comparison descends this reduction to a bounded constructible étale $A$-complex $C$. All constant-field module sheaves are flat, so tensoring $C$ with any module preserves its cohomological interval. Apply the adic criterion (2)$\Rightarrow$(1), then the reverse integral model comparison: $H$ is bounded constructible in the required general-lfp sense.

source.place: Tag 09AI, constructible comparison; Tag 09C0, section-suitable-derived, through the cited criterion. Flatness uses the cited constant-field theorem, whose sources are sites-modules.tex, Tags 03ER/08FC, and fields.tex, Tag 09FN.

proof.text: For integral bounded constructible $K_0,L_0$, the model comparison supplies continuity of internal Hom on common-lower-bound diagrams. The module category has exact filtered colimits. Apply the localization comparison with $s=\ell$ and $B[1/\ell]=E_X$: $(R\mathcal Hom_B(K_0,L_0))_E\simeq R\mathcal Hom_{E_X}((K_0)_E,(L_0)_E)$.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and Proposition 6.8.14(2), pp. 61–62; the internal-sheaf sequential-continuity input is separately cited, not attributed to the global Hom lemma.

proof.text: Rationalization supplies integral representatives for arbitrary bounded constructible $E_X$-complexes $K,L$. Steps 5–6 and preservation under scalar extension prove the finite-extension case.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), pp. 61–62; essential surjectivity and compatibility with localization, using def-sfb-rationalization-equivalence.

proof.text: For rational coefficients, both point pullback definitions agree termwise. Field-lfp local triviality applied on each Noetherian stratum makes general-lfp cohomology have finite scalar models $E^r$. Thus internal-Hom continuity applies to every bounded constructible $E_X$-complex.

source.place: Section 6.8 and Remark 6.8.15, via the separately cited coefficient-specific local-triviality theorem; equality of coefficient pullback constructions is checked directly from the two definitions.

proof.text: Descend $K,L$ over $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}$ to one finite $E$, using a compositum and scalar extension. Finite $F/E$ form a small cofinal filtered poset; $F_X$ is finite free and its colimit is $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}$. Step 8 and exact filtered colimits verify the filtered-Hom comparison hypotheses. It identifies the desired Hom with extension of $H_E$, bounded constructible by step 7; preservation under extension to the closure finishes.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15; the algebraic-closure two-colimit and evaluation-normalized filtered Hom comparison are the separate explicitly cited nodes.

proof_origin.place: Assembly using Proposition 6.8.11(3), Lemma 6.8.12, Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15; local completeness is the existing Stacks 099A node. The additional internal continuity and scalar comparisons remain explicitly cited DAG obligations.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q40-28a1fb640 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: FIX, with one change: step 4 now cites sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison. The finite-field Hom node needs pro-étale inputs whose cohomology has finite constant local models. Step 4 applied it to K_1 = K⊗A_X ≅ ν^*C_K and L_1 ≅ ν^*C_L without that citation; the comparison theorem is what says ν^* of a constructible étale A-sheaf has such models. The corrected step 4 is 452 characters, and the corrected item is in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-six-functors-basics/. I read the whole delivery: the item, the new node lem-sfb-internal-hom-localization-comparison and the statements of all 27 cited nodes. The human re-split note of 2026-10-21 is met: the 12006-character proof is now a 9-step, 2789-character assembly (longest step 457) and the statement is unchanged. Live still has the old 10-step proof, so the delivery is not superseded, and nothing cited is on the dropped route list. There is no cycle: neither the item nor the new node is reachable from its own dependencies. Step checks: (1) the norm is fixed by the algebraic embedding and uniqueness of the extended absolute value; (2) the setting is Noetherian, O_E is a DVR with finite residue field of characteristic ℓ, and O_{E,X} is the inverse limit; (3) the integral model comparison and the adic criterion (1)⇒(2) apply, with torsion allowed; (4) the Hom reduction holds for arbitrary K, L at n=1, and Hom into a locally complete object is locally complete (Stacks 099A, same notion as the criterion); (5) the comparison D^b_c(X_ét) ≃ D_bc and flatness of all modules over a field give finite Tor amplitude, then the criterion (2)⇒(1) and the reverse model comparison apply; (6) the continuity node (Noetherian X, common lower bound) and exactness of filtered colimits (Grothendieck category) let the new node apply with s=ℓ; (7) the rationalization equivalence plus scalar-extension preservation, with no circularity; (8) the two point pullbacks are the same construction and lfp local triviality gives free E^r models; (9) the Q̄ two-colimit, a compositum, finite-free F_X and the filtered-Hom node, using only its statement. Sources checked: Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 3.4.11, 6.7.13, 6.8.11–6.8.15 (pp. 60–62), and Stacks 01T6, 09GU, 099A, 09AI, 09C0, 03ER, 08FC, 09FN. The new node passes B1–B9: it is statement-only, self-contained and has 7 recorded searches. Its from.node is null, which is what blueprint_refs ancestor prints. Its statement is true: the telescope S is flat, continuity on the s-diagram of a bounded-below L gives S⊗H ≅ H(K,S⊗L), and scalar adjunction plus conservativity of restriction finish. I tested it with s=0, 1 or invertible, K=0, L=0 and a one-object site. It duplicates no existing node: the filtered-colimit node needs finite-free algebras, not an s-module telescope; the pbc scalar-localization node is about global Hom groups; the trf flat base change node is for one-object sites and pseudo-coherent E. It is not a clause of the item. The 17 declared tool uses are accepted as generic. Advisory: the report says the SGA 4½ text in source.external was replaced, but it is still there. It is blueprint-owned metadata, which review_split exempts from the route lock, and no proof step cites SGA.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
